name: Recipe generation — ingredients to three recipes

nodes.name: POST /generate-recipe (from Angular app)
nodes.notes: POST /webhook/generate-recipe. Body is the RecipeRequest from src/app/core/recipe-request.ts.

nodes.name: Validate request
nodes.notes: Checklist requirement: revalidate the frontend's input before the paid model is reached.

nodes.name: Return 400 – invalid request
nodes.notes: Answers 400 with the concrete reasons instead of failing the run.

nodes.name: Resolve client IP and date
nodes.notes: Same logic as the quota lookup workflow. Broken IP detection falls back to the system-wide counter.

nodes.name: Hash client IP
nodes.notes: HMAC-SHA256 of the IP with the secret from the 'Quota IP hash salt' credential. Only this hash is used as the Firebase key, so stored quota data cannot be turned back into an address without the secret.

nodes.name: Read today's counters
nodes.notes: The /quota subtree is denied to clients by database rule; only this service account reads it.

nodes.name: Check quota
nodes.notes: Cost airbag before the model call: 3 per IP per day, 12 system-wide.

parameters.responseBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ error: $json.systemLimitReached ? "The daily limit for everyone is reached. Please try again tomorrow." : "You used all 3 recipe generations for today. Please try again tomorrow.", quota: { remaining: 0, limit: $json.limit, systemLimitReached: $json.systemLimitReached } }) }}

nodes.name: Return 429 – daily quota used up
nodes.notes: 429 with a message the user can act on, distinguishing the personal from the system-wide limit.

nodes.name: Build prompt
nodes.notes: Cardinality rules are repeated in the prompt because the API only guarantees syntactically valid JSON.

nodes.name: Generate recipes
nodes.notes: Gemini 3.5 Flash Lite: 15 requests per minute and 500 per day on the free tier, against 20 per day for the non-Lite models. 'Output Content as JSON' sets responseMimeType application/json; this node has no response schema option, so the shape is requested in the prompt and verified afterwards. Reads the prompt by node name because a retry arrives here from 'Retry Gemini once?', not from 'Build prompt'.

nodes.name: Parse and verify recipes
nodes.notes: Enforces what the schema cannot: exactly three recipes, at most three missing ingredients, matching cuisine/diet/time, steps renumbered, assignedTo within the helper count, nutrition present. Throws otherwise, which reaches the error workflow.

nodes.name: Store recipes
nodes.notes: Runs once per recipe because the previous node emits three items. Firebase POST generates the key and returns it as body.name - that key becomes the recipe id.

nodes.name: Collect ids and raise counters
nodes.notes: Gathers the three generated Firebase keys and prepares the new quota counters.

nodes.name: Raise quota counters
nodes.notes: PATCH merges both counters in one call. Deliberately after the recipes are stored: a failed write must not consume quota.

nodes.name: Build response
nodes.notes: Returns the three recipes with their ids plus the remaining quota, matching GenerateRecipesResponse in src/app/core/recipe.ts.

nodes.name: Return 200 – three recipes to app
nodes.notes: Answers 200 with the three stored recipes, their ids and the remaining quota.

nodes.name: Retry Gemini once?
nodes.notes: Second attempt after the model failed or its reply did not pass verification. $runIndex is this node's own run count, so it lets exactly one retry through: at most two Gemini calls per request. Quota is only raised after storing, so a retry is never counted twice.

parameters.responseBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ error: "Recipe generation failed. Please try again." }) }}

nodes.name: Return 500 – generation failed
nodes.notes: Without this the webhook (response mode: Respond to Webhook node) never answers a failed run and the frontend spinner runs until its own timeout.

nodes.name: Fail run → error workflow emails admin
nodes.notes: Fails the run after the visitor got the 500, so the error workflow still mails the original error.

parameters.content:
## POST /webhook/generate-recipe
Called by the Angular app on **/generator/loading** (`RecipeApi.generate()`) with the ingredients and preferences.

**Possible answers**
- **200** three stored recipes with ids + remaining quota
- **400** request failed validation (`details` lists why)
- **429** daily quota used up (per IP or system-wide)
- **500** generation or storing failed, see error path

Every failure after the quota check also mails the admin via the error workflow.

## 1. Validate request
Re-checks the request before the paid model is reached; invalid input gets a 400 with reasons.

## 2. Quota check (hashed IP)
IP is HMAC-hashed, never stored. 3 per IP and 12 system-wide per day, read from Firebase /quota/<date>.

## 3. Gemini + verification (1 retry)
Gemini in JSON mode, then the reply is parsed and checked. A failure in either node gets one retry.

## 4. Store + respond
Stores the three recipes, raises the quota counters (only now, so failures cost no quota) and answers 200.

## Error path
Five nodes have their error output wired here: **Generate recipes**, **Parse and verify recipes**, **Store recipes**, **Collect ids and raise counters**, **Raise quota counters**.
- Gemini / parse failures go to **Retry Gemini once?** first: one retry, at most two Gemini calls. The second failure goes on to the 500.
- Store and counter failures are not retried (writes are not atomic) and go straight to the 500.
- **Return 500** answers the app, then **Fail run** stops with an error. Because Settings → Error Workflow points at the error handler, that failed run triggers the alert email to the admin.

main.node: Fail run → error workflow emails admin
